content.title: About
content.content: Chinese cabbage (Brassica rapa subsp. pekinensis) is an annual leafy vegetable widely used in Asian cuisine. Fresh leaves are crisp, mildly sweet, and aromatic. It is eaten raw in salads and also used for pickling and fermenting.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Chinese cabbage originates from East Asia and was introduced to Europe in the 17th century.
Unlike regular white cabbage, its leaves are softer, light‑green and often slightly wavy.
It is a rich source of vitamin C: 100 g of fresh product provides about 45 mg of vitamin C.
Commonly used in traditional dishes such as kimchi and the Chinese salad “paocai”.
Leaves can be used as wrappers for stuffed dishes.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C supports the immune system, aids collagen synthesis, and acts as an antioxidant.

items.title: Contains vitamin K
items.content: Vitamin K is essential for blood clotting and bone health.

items.title: Low‑calorie food
items.content: Cabbage is low in calories, making it a great choice for weight management.

items.title: Source of dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber improves digestion, promotes satiety, and supports gut microbiota.

items.title: Contains glucosinolates
items.content: These compounds may have anti‑inflammatory and anticancer properties.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to cabbage, such as skin rash or swelling.

items.title: Thyroid concerns
items.content: Large amounts of raw cabbage can affect iodine absorption in people with hypothyroidism.

items.title: Bacterial contamination
items.content: Improperly washed cabbage may harbor pathogenic bacteria, so it should be rinsed thoroughly.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Chinese cabbage is enjoyed raw in salads, often dressed with soy sauce, sesame oil, and ginger. It can be added to wraps, sandwiches, or used as a base for a light marinate. If desired, briefly blanch the leaves to soften their texture.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cabbage in the refrigerator in a perforated bag or a container with a small amount of moisture. Properly stored, it stays fresh for 1‑2 weeks. Remove wilted leaves to extend shelf life.

chicken-breast-baked-coated-skin-coating.title: Chicken breast, baked, coated, skin/coating eaten

content.title: About
content.content: Chicken breast is a lean, boneless cut taken from the bird’s chest. In this product the breast is baked after being coated with breadcrumbs, spices and sometimes a thin layer of oil, leaving the coating edible. The method keeps the meat juicy while creating a crispy crust.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Chicken breast is the most consumed chicken cut worldwide due to its low cost and high nutritional value.
Baking in a coating retains more moisture than pan‑frying.
Coating chicken with breadcrumbs became popular in 19th‑century Europe as a way to make inexpensive meat more satisfying.
Coatings can include breadcrumbs, ground nuts, Parmesan, or herbs, allowing many flavor variations.
Skin‑less chicken breast provides about 31 g of protein and less than 5 g of fat per 100 g.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: Chicken breast supplies high‑quality protein essential for muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: When baked without excessive oil, it remains a low‑calorie protein source.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: It provides niacin (B3) and vitamin B6, which support metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Source of minerals
items.content: Chicken contains phosphorus, selenium and zinc, important for bones and immunity.

items.title: Promotes satiety
items.content: The high protein content helps keep you feeling full for longer.

items.title: Food‑borne illness risk
items.content: Undercooked chicken may harbor Salmonella; cook to an internal temperature of 75 °C (165 °F).

items.title: Allergy to coating ingredients
items.content: Some people are allergic to wheat, dairy or nuts that may be used in the breading.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: If the coating contains salt or soy sauce, intake should be limited for hypertension.

items.title: Caloric coating
items.content: The crispy crust adds extra calories and fat, especially when oil is used.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Baked coated chicken breast can be served as a main dish, sliced for salads, added to sandwiches, or paired with vegetables and whole‑grain sides. Let it rest a few minutes after cooking so the juices redistribute.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep raw breast in the refrigerator at 0‑4 °C for up to 2 days. Cooked portions store in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 3 days or freeze for up to 2 months. Reheat to an internal temperature of 75 °C before eating.

content.title: About
content.content: Grilled bass fillet is a tender, lean white fish with a subtle nutty flavor. Bass is farmed in clean lakes and rivers, and grilling preserves most of its nutrients while adding a smoky aroma.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Bass belongs to the Percidae family and is one of the most popular grill fish in Europe and North America.
Its omega‑3 fatty acid content is higher than many marine fish because of a diet rich in algae.
Traditionally, whole bass is grilled over open fire, but fillets are more convenient for quick cooking.
In Japan, bass fillets are often marinated in soy sauce and lemon juice before grilling to enhance flavor.
Bass can grow up to 2.5 kg, but most commercial fillets come from fish weighing 0.5–1 kg.

items.title: Rich in omega‑3 fatty acids
items.content: Omega‑3s support heart health, lower triglyceride levels, and have anti‑inflammatory properties.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: Bass fillet provides all essential amino acids, aiding muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Compared with many sea fish, bass has a modest fat content, making it suitable for calorie‑controlled diets.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: Vitamin B12, B6 and niacin help maintain nervous system function and energy metabolism.

items.title: Minerals: selenium and phosphorus
items.content: Selenium protects cells from oxidative stress, while phosphorus is essential for bone and tooth health.

items.title: Fish allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to fish, ranging from skin rashes to anaphylaxis.

items.title: Heavy metal contamination
items.content: Although bass generally contains low mercury levels, it is advisable to source fish from clean waters.

items.title: Possible parasites
items.content: Insufficient cooking can leave parasites alive; ensure the internal temperature reaches at least 63 °C.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve grilled bass fillet hot, drizzled with lemon juice or a sauce made from olive oil and fresh herbs. It pairs well with roasted vegetables, quinoa, mashed potatoes, or a crisp salad. For extra tenderness, marinate the fillet beforehand in a mixture of lemon, garlic, and rosemary.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep fresh bass fillets in the refrigerator at 0–2 °C, wrapped in plastic film or in an airtight container, for up to 2 days. For longer storage, freeze at –18 °C in a sealed bag, where they retain quality for up to 3 months. Thaw in the fridge before cooking; discard if the fish smells sour or feels slimy.

content.title: About
content.content: Bass fillet (NFS) is a tender white meat from freshwater bass raised in controlled aquaculture conditions. It has a mild, slightly sweet flavor and a firm yet flaky texture. The fillets are usually sold vacuum‑packed and ready for cooking.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Bass is one of the most popular freshwater fish in Russia and the CIS countries.
In the wild bass can reach up to 1.5 kg, but farmed specimens are typically 300–500 g.
Bass meat contains very few bones, making it convenient for children and people with chewing difficulties.
Bass belongs to the Percidae family; its scientific name is *Perca fluviatilis*.
In Japan bass is often used for sushi and sashimi, while in Russia it is more commonly pan‑fried or baked.

items.title: Rich in omega‑3 fatty acids
items.content: Bass provides EPA and DHA, which support heart and brain health.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: A 100 g serving contains about 20 g of complete animal protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Source of vitamin D
items.content: Vitamin D aids calcium absorption and supports the immune system.

items.title: Contains selenium
items.content: Selenium is a potent antioxidant and helps thyroid function.

items.title: Low in saturated fat
items.content: Makes bass suitable for low‑fat dietary plans.

items.title: Fish allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to bass.

items.title: Contamination risk
items.content: Like other fish, bass can contain trace amounts of heavy metals; purchase from reputable sources.

items.title: Purine content
items.content: High purine levels may exacerbate gout symptoms.

items.title: Need for proper cooking
items.content: Raw bass fillet may harbor parasites; cook to an internal temperature of at least 63 °C.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Bass fillet can be pan‑fried, baked, steamed, or poached in broth. For extra flavor, marinate in lemon juice, olive oil, and herbs for 15–30 minutes before cooking.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the fillet in its original vacuum pack in the refrigerator at +2…4 °C for up to 3 days. For longer storage, freeze in an airtight bag at –18 °C for up to 2 months. Discard if it develops an ammonia‑like odor.

content.title: About
content.content: French toast is a dish made from slices of bread soaked in a mixture of eggs, milk, and spices, then fried until golden brown. It is often served with syrup, berries, powdered sugar, or butter. In fast‑food restaurants it is prepared quickly using pre‑mixed batters and pre‑sliced bread.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The dish originated in France in the 17th century but became popular in the United States in the early 20th century.
Traditional recipes include cinnamon and vanilla, while modern versions may add banana, chocolate, or nuts.
French toast is commonly served for breakfast but can also appear on lunch and dinner menus.
In some countries it is called “egg toast” or “golden toast.”
Fast preparation is achieved by using ready‑made egg‑milk mixes.

items.title: Protein source
items.content: Eggs provide complete protein essential for tissue repair.

items.title: Contains calcium
items.content: Milk and occasional cheese add calcium important for bones and teeth.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Eggs and milk are rich in B2, B6, and B12, supporting energy metabolism.

items.title: Energy boost
items.content: Carbohydrates from the bread supply quick energy, useful for active people.

items.title: Antioxidants in spices
items.content: Cinnamon and vanilla contain polyphenols with antioxidant properties.

items.title: High calorie content
items.content: Butter and syrup can significantly increase the dish’s calorie count.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Added sweeteners may be problematic for people with diabetes.

items.title: Egg or milk allergy
items.content: Individuals with food allergies may react to these ingredients.

items.title: Gluten in bread
items.content: Traditional bread contains gluten, making the dish unsuitable for those with celiac disease.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve French toast hot, drizzled with maple syrup, fruit sauce, or dusted with powdered sugar. It can be topped with fresh fruit, nuts, yogurt, or bacon for a more filling option.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Prepared French toast is best eaten immediately. If needed, cool it in an airtight container for up to 2 days and reheat in an oven or toaster. Do not keep it longer than 3 days to avoid loss of flavor and texture.

content.title: About
content.content: Similac Advance Ready-to-Feed is a infant formula designed for babies from birth to 12 months. It contains whole cow’s milk, fermented lactose, prebiotics, DHA, ARA, and a full spectrum of vitamins and minerals needed for growth and development.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Similac Advance is manufactured by Abbott, one of the world’s largest infant nutrition companies.
The formula is enriched with DHA and ARA – fatty acids that support brain and eye development.
It includes prebiotics (PDX and GOS) to promote a healthy gut microbiome.
Ready-to-Feed format requires no mixing with water, making it convenient for travel and situations without clean water.
The product has undergone clinical testing and meets the recommendations of the American Academy of Pediatrics.

items.title: Bone growth support
items.content: Contains calcium, phosphorus and vitamin D, which together help build strong bones and teeth.

items.title: Brain and eye development
items.content: DHA and ARA are structural components of brain tissue and retinal cells, supporting their normal development.

items.title: Healthy gut flora
items.content: Prebiotics PDX and GOS stimulate the growth of beneficial bacteria, improving digestion and immunity.

items.title: Energy provision
items.content: A balanced mix of protein, fat and carbohydrates provides a steady source of energy for rapid growth.

items.title: Vitamin‑mineral complex
items.content: B‑vitamins, vitamin C, iron and zinc support immune function and metabolic processes.

items.title: Cow‑milk allergy
items.content: Infants with a confirmed cow‑milk protein allergy may react to this formula and should not use it.

items.title: Lactose content
items.content: Babies with lactose intolerance may experience discomfort; a lactose‑free formula should be chosen instead.

items.title: Shelf‑life after opening
items.content: Once opened, the product should be refrigerated at +2–4 °C and used within 48 hours.

items.title: Not a complete substitute for breast milk
items.content: While nutritionally complete, breast milk remains the preferred source of nutrition during the first six months.

content.title: How to Use
content.content: Serve the ready‑to‑feed formula directly from the container, warming gently to body temperature if desired (no more than 37 °C). Do not microwave, as it can create hot spots.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store unopened containers in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. After opening, keep refrigerated and use within 48 hours. Discard if the product develops an off‑smell, color change, or unusual taste.

content.title: About
content.content: Pizza with pepperoni and stuffed crust is a classic Italian‑style pizza topped with tomato sauce, mozzarella cheese, and slices of spicy pepperoni sausage. The crust is filled with a buttery cheese blend, making it extra juicy and crunchy.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Pepperoni is an American version of Italian salami that became popular in the United States in the early 20th century.
Stuffed‑crust pizza was introduced in the 1990s as a way to add extra cheesy flavor without increasing the amount of cheese on top.
Traditional pizza is baked in a wood‑fired oven at 400–500 °C, giving it a distinctive aroma and crisp crust.
The combination of spicy pepperoni and a creamy cheese‑filled crust creates a flavor contrast loved by many fans of bold foods.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: Pepperoni provides animal protein, which is essential for tissue repair and muscle maintenance.

items.title: Calcium from cheese
items.content: Mozzarella and the cheese filling are good sources of calcium, supporting bone health.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: The sausage and dough contain B1, B2, and B6 vitamins important for metabolism.

items.title: Energy dense
items.content: Pizza delivers a quick supply of calories, useful during periods of high physical activity.

items.title: Lycopene from tomatoes
items.content: Tomato sauce is rich in lycopene, an antioxidant that may support heart health.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Pepperoni and sauce often contain a lot of salt, which can be problematic for hypertension.

items.title: Saturated fats
items.content: Cheese and processed meat are high in saturated fats, which may raise cholesterol when consumed in excess.

items.title: Dairy allergy or lactose intolerance
items.content: People with milk protein allergy or lactose intolerance should choose alternative options.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: A single slice can contain 300–500 kcal, so portion control is advisable.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Slice the pizza into even pieces and serve hot. Fresh basil or arugula can be added for brightness, and an extra sprinkle of grated Parmesan is optional.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2–3 days. Reheat in an oven or grill to keep the crust crisp.

content.title: About
content.content: Potato Tots NFS (item 4271) are small fried bites made from grated potato, breadcrumbs and seasonings. They have a crispy golden crust and a soft, slightly creamy interior. The product is designed for quick preparation in an oven or deep‑fryer and is commonly used as a snack or side dish.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Potato tots first appeared in the United States in the 1950s as a convenient way to use leftover potatoes.
The NFS brand is known for consistent flavor and texture across batches.
A small amount of corn starch is often added to make the tots extra crunchy.
They are frequently served with ranch dressing or ketchup in fast‑food settings.
Each 200 g package contains roughly 30–35 tots.

items.title: Source of carbohydrates
items.content: Potato tots provide a quick source of energy thanks to easily digestible carbs.

items.title: Contains vitamin C
items.content: A modest amount of vitamin C survives rapid frying, supporting the immune system.

items.title: Potassium
items.content: Potatoes are rich in potassium, important for fluid balance and muscle function.

items.title: Low sugar content
items.content: Unlike sweet snacks, tots have low levels of simple sugars.

items.title: Portion control
items.content: Their bite‑size shape helps manage calorie intake.

items.title: High fat content
items.content: When fried, tots absorb oil, increasing calories and saturated fat levels.

items.title: Sodium
items.content: Salt content can be high, which may be unsuitable for hypertension.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: Breadcrumbs often contain wheat; people with celiac disease should choose a gluten‑free version.

items.title: Trans fats
items.content: Using partially hydrogenated oils can lead to the formation of trans fats.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Cook the tots in a preheated oven at 200 °C for 12–15 minutes or deep‑fry for 3–4 minutes until golden. Serve hot with a dip, in burgers, salads, or as a standalone snack.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the unopened package in a dry, cool place away from direct light. After opening, transfer the tots to an airtight container and use within 5–7 days. Discard if a rancid oil smell develops.

content.title: About
content.content: Salsa verde is a classic Mexican sauce made from fresh tomatillos, chilies, onion, garlic, cilantro and lime. It has a bright, slightly tangy and spicy flavor that pairs perfectly with tacos, nachos, grilled meats and seafood.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Salsa verde is traditionally served cold, but it can also be gently warmed.
Tomatillos are rich in antioxidants such as vitamin C and carotenoids.
The original recipe uses only fresh cilantro, though some regions add parsley.
The heat level can range from mild to very hot depending on the type and amount of chilies used.

items.title: High in vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C supports the immune system and aids iron absorption.

items.title: Low‑calorie sauce
items.content: Salsa verde is low in calories, making it a great choice for weight‑conscious diets.

items.title: Antioxidant content
items.content: Tomatillos and lime provide antioxidants that help combat free radicals.

items.title: Digestive aid
items.content: Cilantro and lime may promote digestion thanks to their natural enzymes.

items.title: Cilantro allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience an allergic reaction to cilantro.

items.title: Spiciness
items.content: Very hot salsa can cause discomfort for people with sensitive stomachs.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: If salt is added, monitor the amount, especially for low‑sodium diets.

content.title: How to Use
content.content: Serve salsa verde with tacos, burritos, nachos, grilled meats, fish, seafood, or use it as a marinade or salad dressing.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the salsa in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 5 days. When frozen, it can last up to 2 months, though the texture may change slightly.
